symbols.name: d
symbols.def: Dimension of each vector potential outcome.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Total sample size and triangular-array index.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: \(K=K_N\) is the number of treatment arms.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m=m_N\) is the common number of observations per arm.

symbols.name: Bd
symbols.def: \(\mathbb B_d=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:\|z\|_2\le 1\}\), the Euclidean unit ball.

symbols.name: Pk
symbols.def: \(P_k\) is the marginal law in arm \(k\in\mathcal I_K\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma(\mathbf P)\) is the set of all \(K\)-couplings with marginals \(P_1,\ldots,P_K\).

symbols.name: zk
symbols.def: \(z_k\) is coordinate \(k\) of a generic tuple \((z_1,\ldots,z_K)\in\mathbb B_d^K\).

symbols.name: fdual
symbols.def: \(f_k\) is coordinate \(k\) of a multi-margin Kantorovich dual tuple.

symbols.name: Fdual
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\), the normalized jointly \(c_K\)-conjugate class defined by \(\mathrm{def:joint-dual-class}\).

symbols.name: BN
symbols.def: \(B_N=B_N((X_{ki})_{k,i})\) is any real-valued statistic intended to lie below \(L(\mathbf P)\).

symbols.name: Rdk
symbols.def: \(R_d(N,K)=\inf_T\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|T-L(\mathbf P)|\).

symbols.name: Halpha
symbols.type: class of honest lower confidence bounds

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: First law in the two-margin reduction.

symbols.name: nu
symbols.def: Second law in the two-margin reduction.

symbols.name: delta0
symbols.def: \(\delta_0\) is the point mass at the origin.

symbols.name: pi2
symbols.def: \(\pi\) is a generic coupling of \(\mu\) and \(\nu\).

symbols.name: Cd
symbols.def: \(C_d\) depends only on the fixed dimension \(d\).

symbols.name: cd
symbols.def: \(c_d\) depends only on the fixed dimension \(d\).

symbols.name: c0
symbols.def: \(c_0\) is a fixed arm-growth threshold constant that may depend on \(d\).

symbols.name: CertMOT
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) returns a primal value, a dual value, and a certified bracket for \(L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\).

symbols.name: Llower
symbols.def: \(\underline L_\epsilon\) is the lower endpoint returned by \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\).

symbols.name: Lupper
symbols.def: \(\overline L_\epsilon\) is the upper endpoint returned by \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\).

symbols.name: rhoest
symbols.def: The exact estimation-rate function DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:exact-all-k-frontier}\).

symbols.name: rholen
symbols.def: The exact honest-length-rate function DERIVED by \(\mathrm{oeq:exact-all-k-frontier}\).

symbols.name: qfrontier
symbols.def: \(q_{\mathrm{fr}}\) is the cardinality of the finite rational support used by the simultaneous-marginal perturbation handle.

symbols.name: Gfrontier
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{q,d}=\{g_1,\ldots,g_{q_{\mathrm{fr}}}\}\subset\mathbb B_d\) is the common support of every perturbed marginal.

symbols.name: ThetaHyp
symbols.type: ordered pair of finite hypothesis index sets
symbols.def: \(\boldsymbol\Theta=(\Theta_0,\Theta_1)\) consists of disjoint finite low-endpoint and high-endpoint index sets.

symbols.name: Ptheta
symbols.type: indexed tuple of finite-support marginal laws
symbols.def: \(\mathbf P_\theta=(P_{1,\theta},\ldots,P_{K,\theta})\) is the simultaneous-marginal perturbation family constructed in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous-perturbation-family}\).

symbols.name: RemGap
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\) is the minimum reduced-cost slack over every rematching column outside the declared contact columns, as constructed in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous-perturbation-family}\).

symbols.name: Hfrontier
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\) denotes the finite-support family \(\mathbf P_\theta\), its observable diagnostics \(\Delta_{N,K}\), \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\), and the alternative jointly normalized \(c_K\)-transform localization.

symbols.name: nSTAR
symbols.def: \(n^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(161,37,36)\) for control, the Student Support Program, and the Student Fellowship Program.

symbols.name: betaSTAR
symbols.def: \(\beta^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(-1,1/2,1/2)\), ordered as control, the Student Support Program, and the Student Fellowship Program.

symbols.name: BSTAR
symbols.def: \(B^{\mathrm{STAR}}<\infty\) is a prespecified bound for the absolute STAR potential outcomes.

symbols.name: YSTAR
symbols.def: \(Y(k)\) is the STAR outcome under cell \(k\in\{1,2,3\}\), with the known bound \(|Y(k)|\le B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\).

symbols.name: bY
symbols.def: \(b_Y=B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\max_{1\le k\le3}|\beta_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}|\) is the known contrast scale.

symbols.name: WSTARj
symbols.def: \(W_j^{\mathrm{STAR}}\) is the assigned STAR cell for unit \(j\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{STAR}}\).

symbols.name: SSTARk
symbols.type: indexed ordered subsample of unit indices
symbols.def: \(S_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(J_{k1},\ldots,J_{k,m^{\mathrm{STAR}}})\) is sampled uniformly without replacement from \(\{j:W_j^{\mathrm{STAR}}=k\}\) by auxiliary randomization independent of all outcomes.

standard.name: Three-arm extension of i.i.d. superpopulation potential-outcome sampling
Complete randomized assignment with fixed treatment-cell counts

definitions.name: MOT triangular-array model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_d=\{(N,K,m,\mathbf P,(X_{ki})_{k\in\mathcal I_K,1\le i\le m}):N=Km,\ \mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K,\ \mathcal L((X_{ki})_{k,i})=\bigotimes_{k=1}^KP_k^{\otimes m},\ m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\}\).

definitions.name: Normalized jointly conjugate dual class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}=\{(f_1,\ldots,f_K):f_k:\mathbb B_d\to\mathbb R,\ f_k(x)=\inf_{(z_\ell)_{\ell\ne k}\in\mathbb B_d^{K-1}}[c_K(z_1,\ldots,z_{k-1},x,z_{k+1},\ldots,z_K)-\sum_{\ell\ne k}f_\ell(z_\ell)]\text{ for every }k,\ f_k(0)=0\text{ for }k<K\}\).

definitions.name: Minimax endpoint risk
definitions.construction: \(R_d(N,K)=\inf_T\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|T-L(\mathbf P)|\).

definitions.name: Uniformly honest lower bounds
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_\alpha=\{B_N:\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}\Pr_{\mathbf P}(B_N\le L(\mathbf P))\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: Minimax expected excess length
definitions.construction: \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)=\inf_{B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+]\).

definitions.name: Fixed-dimensional certified empirical MOT procedure
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) quantizes each empirical atom to a rational grid of mesh at most \(\epsilon/(8\sqrt d)\), solves the gridded dual by the ellipsoid method with a dynamic-programming separation oracle indexed by partial sums, lifts a primal coupling through quantization fibers, and returns the primal--dual bracket enlarged by the deterministic quantization error.

definitions.name: Finite-support simultaneous-marginal perturbation handle
definitions.construction: Fix \(\mathcal G_{q,d}=\{g_1,\ldots,g_{q_{\mathrm{fr}}}\}\subset\mathbb B_d\). Choose an integer \(s\), positive rational baseline masses \(p_{kj}\), a rational amplitude \(\delta>0\), and signed directions \(h_{k\ell j}\) satisfying \(\sum_jh_{k\ell j}=0\) and \(p_{kj}+\delta\sum_{\ell=1}^s\theta_\ell h_{k\ell j}\ge0\). For each \(\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\), set \(P_{k,\theta}=\sum_{j=1}^{q_{\mathrm{fr}}}[p_{kj}+\delta\sum_{\ell=1}^s\theta_\ell h_{k\ell j}]\delta_{g_j}\) and \(\mathbf P_\theta=(P_{1,\theta},\ldots,P_{K,\theta})\). Solve each finite primal--dual MOT pair; for its declared contact-column set \(\mathcal C_\theta\) and dual tuple \(f^\theta\), record \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}=\min_{\theta}\min_{(j_1,\ldots,j_K)\notin\mathcal C_\theta}[c_K(g_{j_1},\ldots,g_{j_K})-\sum_{k=1}^Kf_k^\theta(g_{j_k})]\), together with \(\Delta_{N,K}\) and \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\).

definitions.name: All-arm frontier handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\) applies the finite family in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous-perturbation-family}\) to seek \(\Delta_{N,K}\) with \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\) and nonnegative reduced-cost slack for every rematching column; its alternative branch derives a shared bound for the jointly \(c_K\)-conjugate tuple by common-support interpolation. Either branch is paired with \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\).

definitions.name: Known-bound STAR scaling and randomized balanced subsample
definitions.construction: Draw \(U_j^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(Y_j(1),Y_j(2),Y_j(3))\) independently from \(Q^{\mathrm{STAR}}\) for \(j\in\mathcal J^{\mathrm{STAR}}\). Independently assign the units by complete randomization with cell counts \(n^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(161,37,36)\). Conditional on the assignment, draw each ordered \(S_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}\) uniformly without replacement with size \(m^{\mathrm{STAR}}=36\), using auxiliary randomness independent of all potential outcomes. Apply the known affine map \(s_{B^{\mathrm{STAR}}}(y)=y/B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\) and set \(X_{ki}^{\mathrm{STAR}}=(\beta_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}Y_{J_{ki}}(k)/b_Y,0,0,0,0)\in\mathbb B_5\), where \(b_Y=B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\max_{1\le\ell\le3}|\beta_\ell^{\mathrm{STAR}}|\).

statements.statement: For every \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_K)\in(2\mathbb B_d)^K\), there exists \(I\subseteq\mathcal I_K\) such that \(\|\sum_{k\in I}a_k-A/2\|_2^2\le r\), where \(A=\sum_{k=1}^Ka_k\) and \(r=\min\{K,d\}\).
statements.justification: This is the dimension-sensitive replacement for summing \(K\) one-coordinate exchange inequalities.
statements.gap: Classical vector balancing supplies extreme-point rounding, but its insertion into the repulsive quadratic MOT support argument is not in Gao--Ge--Qian.
statements.consumer: The arbitrary-subset support exchange in Theorem 3 uses this bound to replace \(\sqrt K\) geometry by \(\sqrt{\min\{K,d\}}\).

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), \(0\le V(\mathbf P)\le r\), and \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K}V(\mathbf P)=r\). Equivalently, \(\sup_{\mathbf P}K^2\{L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\}=\min\{K,d\}\).
statements.justification: The exact deterministic distance from the mean floor governs the large-arm transition before any empirical-process analysis begins.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian's Lemma D.2 yields a dimension-blind order bound on optimal sums; Wang--Wang characterize joint mixability only for selected univariate families.
statements.consumer: A causal analyst can certify when the unidentified second-moment improvement over the mean floor is uniformly too small to justify solving MOT.

statements.statement: For every optimizer \(\gamma^{\star}\in\Gamma(\mathbf P)\), \(\operatorname{diam}\{\sum_{k=1}^Kz_k:(z_1,\ldots,z_K)\in\operatorname{supp}(\gamma^{\star})\}\le2\sqrt r\); the constant is attained when \(K\ge d\) by orthogonal symmetric two-point margins.
statements.justification: This support theorem is the shared geometry needed to localize all dual potentials at once.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian exchange one coordinate and obtain a \(\sqrt K\)-scale control; no located source gives the sharp fixed-dimensional diameter for this repulsive sum cost.
statements.consumer: The empirical-process upper bound uses the diameter to normalize dual slopes by \(K^{-2}\sqrt r\).

statements.statement: For \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{hyp}}=(H_d,\ldots,H_d)\), \(L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{hyp}})=0\) when \(K\) is even and \(L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{hyp}})=K^{-2}\) when \(K\) is odd. In particular, the legal \(K=3,d=5\) witness satisfies \(L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{hyp}})=1/9\).
statements.justification: Parity is a complete all-rematching certificate and a destructive check against treating vector joint mixability as automatic.
statements.gap: The mixability literature studies selected scalar classes; the explicit vector hypercube law and its original second-moment endpoint are not supplied by those results.
statements.consumer: The \(K=3,d=5\) instance provides an exact finite benchmark for every empirical MOT and dual-certificate implementation.

statements.statement:
After substituting \(P_1=\mu\), \(P_2=(-\operatorname{Id})_{\#}
u\), and \(P_3=\cdots=P_K=\delta_0\) into the definition of \(L\), one has definitionally \(K^2L(\mathbf P)=\inf_{\pi\in\Gamma(\mu,
u)}\int\|x-y\|_2^2\,d\pi(x,y)=W_2^2(\mu,
u)\).
statements.justification: This sanity-reduction helper checks normalization and transfers the published two-margin obstruction; it is not counted as a research contribution.
statements.gap: The identity is a direct definitional specialization, so no novelty is claimed for it; the unresolved work is the genuinely all-arm rematching obstruction.
statements.consumer: The exact-frontier question must dominate the scaled two-margin modulus and preserve its fixed-\(K\) logarithmic issue.

statements.statement: There is \(C_d<\infty\) such that \(\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,\ K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\). Relative to Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1, the cap improves from \(K^{-1}\) to \(rK^{-2}\), strictly when \(K>d\), and the active high-dimensional term improves from \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\) to \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\).
statements.justification: The first theorem-level advance sharpens the published plug-in guarantee using shared squared-sum geometry rather than separate arm envelopes.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 gives \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\) when \(d>4\); no located closer paper proves the displayed \(r\)-controlled bound for arbitrary marginals.
statements.consumer: The rate determines how much sampling uncertainty must be deducted from an empirical causal lower endpoint.

statements.statement: For constants \(0<c_d\le C_d<\infty\), \(c_d\max\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\). The lower maximum is obtained from two distinct submodels and is not attributed to the printed minimum in Gao--Ge--Qian Proposition 2.
statements.justification: The honest sandwich exposes every currently verified polynomial and logarithmic gap instead of promoting the plug-in upper bound to a minimax answer.
statements.gap: Manole--Niles-Weed leave logarithmic slack even for the two-margin all-estimator lower bound, while Gao--Ge--Qian do not close the \(d>4\) all-\(K\) frontier.
statements.consumer: A solver can see exactly which arm-count and logarithmic factors need a new construction rather than re-proving settled root-\(N\) behavior.

statements.statement: There are constants \(c_d,C_d,c_0>0\) such that \(c_dN^{-1/2}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2)\); hence \(R_d(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) uniformly along every legal array satisfying \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\).
statements.justification: The exact root-\(N\) region is already obtainable from deterministic geometry and a mean-driven Le Cam experiment.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian establish minimax optimality only for \(d\le4\); the theorem supplies an unrestricted \(d>4\) growing-arm region without density assumptions.
statements.consumer: Studies with many outcome regimes can bypass a prohibitively large MOT problem and estimate the endpoint at the parametric rate.

statements.statement: For constants \(0<c_{d,\alpha}\le C_{d,\alpha}<\infty\), \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2)\), and \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\). Consequently \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\).
statements.justification: Uniform coverage and expected shortfall are treated as a decision problem distinct from point estimation.
statements.gap: Ji--Lei--Spector prove broad dual-feasible uniform validity, and Manole--Balakrishnan--Wasserman prove near-minimax intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance; neither gives this all-arm one-sided endpoint-length converse.
statements.consumer: A reported MOT tightening can be accompanied by a lower confidence endpoint whose worst-case conservatism is quantitatively controlled.

statements.statement: For fixed \(d\), rational empirical input, and \(0<\epsilon<1\), \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) returns \(\underline L_\epsilon\le L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\le\overline L_\epsilon\) with \(\overline L_\epsilon-\underline L_\epsilon\le\epsilon\), together with primal and dual witnesses, in time polynomial in the input bit length, \(N\), and \((K/\epsilon)^d\).
statements.justification: A statistical rate is operational only if numerical error is separated from sampling error by an auditable certificate.
statements.gap: Generic discrete MOT has \(m^K\) columns and generic pairwise MOT is hard; existing entropic solvers certify regularized or approximate objectives without this fixed-\(d\) squared-sum bracket.
statements.consumer: The empirical lower endpoint and its confidence correction can report a numerical error budget rather than silently absorbing Sinkhorn bias.

statements.statement: Under Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:star-iid-superpopulation}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:star-complete-randomization}\), the randomized balanced subsample in Definition \(\mathrm{def:star-transformation}\) satisfies \(\mathcal L((X_{ki}^{\mathrm{STAR}})_{1\le k\le3,1\le i\le36})=\bigotimes_{k=1}^3(P_k^{\mathrm{STAR}})^{\otimes36}\). It therefore has \(N=108\), \(K=3\), \(m=36\), and \(d=5\), and \(\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})}\mathbb E_\gamma\|\sum_{k=1}^3Z_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}\|_2^2=9L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})\). Consequently, \(9b_Y^2L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})\) is the sharp lower endpoint for \(\mathbb E[(\sum_{k=1}^3\beta_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}Y(k))^2]\). This empirical audit is conditional on the declared i.i.d. superpopulation law, the known bound \(B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\), the affine scaling, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; it does not validate the native-count \((161,37,36)\) plug-in calculation.
statements.justification: The audit separates the estimand-preserving scale transformation from the sampling contract actually required by the theory.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian's theoretical display is balanced, while its public STAR computation uses native unequal cell sizes and does not supply this known-bound scaling plus superpopulation-to-product-law reduction.
statements.consumer: A reanalysis of the scholarship-incentive contrast can state exactly which observations, scale, and endpoint its guarantee covers.

statements.statement: Can the rational finite-support family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous-perturbation-family}\) be chosen so that \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), \(\Delta_{N,K}>0\) has explicit \(K\), \(d\), and logarithmic order, and every alternative rematching column has certified nonnegative reduced cost \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\), with strict slack away from the declared contact columns? If no such additive-complexity family exists, does \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\) instead admit a two-sided localized covering or Rademacher bound controlled by \(r=\min\{K,d\}\)?
statements.justification: This dichotomy is the genuine proof boundary behind the remaining small-\(K\) minimax gap.
statements.gap: Hundrieser--Staudt--Munk transfer entropy between two \(c\)-conjugate potentials, while no located result controls a simultaneous \(K\)-tuple for the repulsive squared-sum cost.
statements.consumer: Resolving the aggregate dual complexity determines whether the empirical MOT estimator is rate-optimal or must be replaced.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\), determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) such that \(R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) uniformly over every legal \(K=K_N\), including exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition. The lower-bound branch must choose the finite-support simultaneous family so that \(\Delta_{N,K}\) matches the claimed rate, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\) certifies the endpoint separation against every rematching column; its ordered low-versus-high version must also support the one-sided length converse. The upper-bound branch must construct a computable estimator and uniformly honest lower bound attaining the respective rates, or prove a sharper shared-geometric dual bound if the simultaneous family cannot achieve the required separation.
statements.justification: The theorem-level kernel is the exact all-arm estimation and honest-length frontier, not merely another plug-in bound.
statements.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian stop at minimax optimality for \(d\le4\); Manole--Niles-Weed leave logarithmic slack for two margins; no closer source found in the 2026 search subsumes the arbitrary-margin endpoint problem.
statements.consumer: The frontier gives a principled uncertainty deduction for every empirical multiworld second-moment lower endpoint, including the scholarship-incentive audit.

sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\) and fixed \(d>4\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are identically distributed from the arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) on \(\mathbb B_d\); all arm samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed experiment supplies one independent sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.6 places a binary covariate-aware mirror-transport lower bound between unconditional and conditional transport, while Theorem 4.3 gives its quadratic-cost plug-in rate under smooth strongly convex Brenier potentials.
The paper proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and derives a direct nonparametric estimator with a convergence rate.
The paper gives a smooth-density wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for binary conditional transport with quadratic cost.
Theorem 22 gives the two-margin all-estimator lower bound \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for quadratic cost.
Theorem 2.2 converts binary \(c\)-transform entropy into two-margin empirical transport rates.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid one-sided inference from any dual-feasible estimated pair in randomized experiments.
The paper constructs finite-sample intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance and bounds their length near the minimax rate.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient joint-mixability conditions for selected classes of univariate distributions.
Donsker dual classes yield two-margin empirical optimal-transport limits given by suprema of Gaussian processes.
Upper and lower Wasserstein dimensions determine multiscale empirical-measure approximation rates.
Quadratic negative-dependence objectives are optimized for selected identical scalar margins admitting a joint mix.

tldr: The lower endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not the centered variance residual. Gao--Ge--Qian identify this endpoint and bound its empirical plug-in risk, but their \(d>4\) theorem leaves both the arm-count frontier and the all-estimator logarithmic gap open, and their support-geometry proof does not exploit fixed dimension. The core derives the exact residual envelope \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), a sharp \(2\sqrt{\min\{K,d\}}\) diameter for optimal sums, and a strictly tighter plug-in upper bound, settling root-\(N\) minimax estimation and honest one-sided excess length for \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The answer-open kernel operationalizes the remaining frontier with a named rational finite-support simultaneous-marginal family whose product-law indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and reduced-cost slack against every rematching column are finite computations; failure of that lower route points to a shared-complexity theorem for jointly conjugate potentials. A fixed-dimensional primal--dual certificate makes the statistical claim computable. The STAR audit is conditional on a known finite outcome bound, an explicit affine scale, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and it does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.

project_justification.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 gives a high-dimensional empirical bound with term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower term with \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and does not establish uniform one-sided coverage or optimal expected excess length. Manole--Niles-Weed leave the same logarithmic all-estimator gap already at two margins. Two-margin entropy transfer and limit theory do not control a growing tuple of jointly conjugate potentials.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry that is absent from generic transport bounds: all potentials obey one constraint, and optimal coupling atoms can be exchanged in arbitrary coordinate subsets. At the same time, a lower construction must survive every alternative multi-arm rematching, so neither a union bound nor a two-margin embedding can decide the rate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter theorems, uses common-support interpolation to tighten the plug-in rate, settles the large-arm root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided length regimes, and poses the precise coupled-complexity dichotomy whose resolution yields the exact all-\(K\) frontier. Its finite-support handle makes indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and resistance to every rematching column explicit certification targets. The procedure returns a primal--dual numerical bracket, and the STAR audit declares the known bound, affine scaling, superpopulation law, randomization, and balanced subsampling.

related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define exactly \(L(\mathbf P)\) in their equation (4), prove the balanced-sample upper rate in Theorem 1, and claim minimax optimality only for \(d\le4\); their Discussion leaves \(d>4\) open. Their supplement localizes each dual potential separately after one-coordinate support exchanges. The upper theorem changes both steps: arbitrary-subset exchanges produce dimension-saturated optimal-sum geometry, and common-support interpolation yields jointly normalized concave potentials. The two-margin identity in Lemma 5 is only a definitional sanity reduction and is not counted toward novelty. Manole and Niles-Weed's Theorem 22 supplies the closest all-estimator lower architecture, but its fuzzy-hypothesis argument gives \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for the two-margin quadratic cost. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's ICML 2025 Proposition 3.6 and Theorem 4.3 study binary covariate-aware causal transport: a mirror-covariate relaxation interpolates between unconditional and conditional bounds and has a plug-in rate under regular Brenier potentials. Their AISTATS 2026 follow-up proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and analyzes a direct nonparametric estimator. Their 2026 smooth-density preprint gives a wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for quadratic binary conditional transport. These covariate-assisted results inform the causal-transport framing but neither tighten nor represent the unconditional arbitrary-margin endpoint with growing \(K\), so the comparator table records them as informed-by rather than extension targets. Hundrieser, Staudt, and Munk show that a binary \(c\)-transform transfers entropy between two potentials; the multi-margin transform depends on all other potentials and has no corresponding tuple contraction. Hundrieser, Klatt, Staudt, and Munk characterize two-margin empirical-cost limits under Donsker dual classes, not the growing-arm high-dimensional transition. Han and Zhu's 2026 two-mode stability theorem assumes regular Monge structure and treats barycentric or uniformly concave sum costs, not the arbitrary-margin repulsive endpoint or its statistical risk. Weed and Bach supply the multiscale quantization background but estimate an empirical measure in Wasserstein distance rather than a smooth MOT value. Wang and Wang characterize zero residual for selected scalar families, while Wang's survey identifies vector mixability and attainable sum laws as open. Koike, Lin, and Wang analyze identical scalar margins and do not cover arbitrary heterogeneous vector laws. Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman derive near-minimax interval lengths for sliced Wasserstein distance through one-dimensional quantiles. Ji, Lei, and Spector derive model-agnostic validity from dual feasibility but no all-arm minimax expected-length converse. Armstrong and Kolesar's ordered modulus motivates the one-sided decision criterion in a linear Gaussian model. Cheryala, Alaya, and Bouzebda establish multi-margin dual attainment and conjugacy without statistical capacity bounds, and Kravtsova treats fixed finite supports rather than arbitrary unit-ball marginals or growing \(K\). Aronow, Green, and Lee prove sharp unequal-allocation variance inference for two arms; their multiple-treatment remark does not supply the unequal three-margin result. Angrist, Lang, and Oreopoulos provide the randomized STAR experiment. Gao--Ge--Qian's application uses native cell sizes \(161,37,36\); the balanced theorem applies to the audit only under the declared i.i.d. superpopulation law, known bound, affine scale, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact small-arm rate remains answer-open. The finite-support perturbation template is operational, but no choice of its support, signed directions, amplitudes, and hypothesis priors is asserted to attain the missing rate: endpoint separation, product-law indistinguishability, and reduced-cost resistance to every rematching column must be established together. The only settled lower helper is the definitional two-margin specialization scaled by \(K^{-2}\), whereas the improved upper theorem can retain a \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) term; tensoring two-margin gadgets in fixed dimension does not bridge that factor because alternative arms can rematch. The official Gao--Ge--Qian supplement also asserts \(\sum_k\|y_1(k)-y_2(k)\|_2^2\le2K\) from unit-ball support, although the displayed support condition alone yields \(4K\); this core therefore re-proves the needed support theorem and does not borrow that step. The certified computation theorem is fixed-dimensional and polynomial in \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a claim of generic polynomial-time exact MOT. The STAR audit discards observations, depends on a known outcome bound and a superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the published numerical tightening.
honest_scope: Every numbered statement is to be proved. The exact residual envelope, optimal-sum diameter, improved empirical upper bound, large-arm minimax claims, computation certificate, and STAR audit are presolve-supported but not treated as established. The exact all-\(K\) rate and the honest one-sided converse are the principal open content; the named simultaneous-marginal family is a construction handle whose required endpoint separation and rematching resistance are not assumed. The proposal makes no density or smoothness assumption, fixes \(d>4\), requires \(m=N/K\to\infty\), and preserves the uncentered second-moment endpoint \(L\). When only two margins are nondegenerate, Lemma 5 is definitionally the ordinary quadratic two-margin transport cost and serves only as a sanity reduction; when \(K\) is fixed, the known sandwich retains the Manole--Niles-Weed logarithmic gap; when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\), Theorems 8 and 9 reduce both decision risks to the familiar root-\(N\) mean problem. For the hypercube special case, Proposition 4 gives zero for even \(K\) and \(K^{-2}\) for odd \(K\), including \(1/9\) at \(K=3,d=5\). The empirical STAR audit is conditional on its declared known-bound scaling and i.i.d. randomized-subsampling model and makes no claim for the native unequal-count computation.

novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level comparator is Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1, which studies the same uncentered endpoint but has the \(d>4\) upper term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\) and cap \(K^{-1}\). Theorem 6 promises a strict deterministic and stochastic tightening to \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) and \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), based on two new cost-specific steps: marginal-preserving extreme-point rounding and arbitrary-subset optimal-support exchanges. Lemma 5 is only the definitional substitution \(K^2L=W_2^2\) and contributes no novelty. Manole--Niles-Weed Theorem 22 is the closest all-estimator lower result, but it is two-marginal, retains \(\log m\), and after embedding is scaled by \(K^{-2}\); the exact all-arm rate is therefore not claimed as an already known formula. The key open question names a rational finite-support family and requires simultaneous verification of mixture indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and reduced-cost slack against every rematching column, or a sharper aggregate dual bound. Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn's ICML 2025 and AISTATS 2026 results, together with their smooth-density inference follow-up, concern covariate-aware binary conditional transport and are recorded only as informed-by comparators to the unconditional arbitrary-margin growing-\(K\) frontier. Ji--Lei--Spector establish validity but not minimax expected excess length; the ordered converse remains an independent contribution. Searches through September 2026 found general MOT conjugacy and fixed-support limit papers, but no closer result subsuming the arbitrary-margin growing-arm frontier.
